about: Emulate round 10 (2026-10-04 04:40 to 04:47 UTC), emulate-runs/community-s5j on the laptop: two calls per unit, raw outputs exact. Inputs: p32 = v51's P32; p26 = P26-c1 (v37's body with "Then there's integration"). Used: p26-emuB (v52's P26 with the meaning put back); p32 not used (v41's P32 passed alone and is closer to the published).

inputs.p32: Communities that are formed during collective spiritual euphoria can recruit too fast and promise too much, and they can end up thinking through how much need they can absorb only once several people already depend on them. Read the sections on capacity and membership, later in this article: they’re partly there to protect the original generosity from that first rush.
inputs.p26: Then there's integration: your life. Ceremony opens something. Did anything change? Look at your life in the weeks after. Look at your relationships, how you behave, how you sleep, how you make decisions, how well you handle frustration without declaring a new spiritual emergency.

p32-emuA: In particular, if (like many of the earliest intentional communities) the core of the community came together in a moment of collective spiritual euphoria, and has not yet had time to consider the needs of a particular large group of potential members before they joined, see later sections of this article for why this may be a problem, and what to do about it.
p32-emuB: Many of the groups that are formed in the heady spiritual euphoria of collective experience make the mistake of expanding to fast and taking on more than they can handle. They don’t get around to thinking about how much need they have the capacity to deal with until they already have a number of people depending on them. Read the sections below on capacity and on membership to see if they’re helpful to avoiding this problem.
p26-emuA: 3. Integration – How has the ceremony fit into your life? Did it open something for you? Look at the last few weeks and see how your life is now, check in with relationships and behavior. Are you sleeping better? Making better decisions? Are you more able to handle frustration without creating a “new spiritual emergency”?
p26-emuB: Integration: How has it affected your life? Did the ceremony open something up in you? Look at your life after the ceremony for a few weeks and see how things have changed, if at all. Look at your relationships, your behavior, your sleeping habits, your decision-making, and how well you can deal with frustration.
